title: Revised tracker data: fewer citation errors, repair remains unresolved
lead: The revised tracker LoRA produced slightly fewer active-intent omissions, but this experiment did not establish the prespecified joint improvement in omission and complete repair over v1. Some uncertainty and withdrawal outcomes worsened.
methods: Three conditions used the same pinned Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct base in one collection process: adapter disabled, tracker v1 and a fresh tracker v2 trained on the revised 500-update dataset. Each condition received the same 200 one-step inputs from 40 new scenario families, including 80 deliberately faulty prior states. Shared prompt, greedy decoding and generation limits were fixed before collection. The primary comparison is v2 versus v1; base and subgroup comparisons are descriptive.
findings: Family-average active concept omission was 2.71% for v1 and 2.06% for v2, a reduction of 0.65 percentage points. The adjusted 97.5% interval was −0.44 to +1.74 points. Complete repair was 19/80 (23.75%) for v1 and 20/80 (25.00%) for v2, a gain of 1.25 points with a 97.5% interval of −8.75 to +11.25. Both intervals cross zero; the joint positive criterion was not met.

Across all 631 active reference units per arm, fully correct coverage was 550 for v1 and 556 for v2; omitted concepts fell from 18 to 14 and wrong values or qualifiers from 35 to 32. Wrong-owner and wrong-status counts stayed at 21 and 9. On ordinary inputs, full active coverage stayed at 335/348, while fully correct targeted reference units fell from 134/148 to 133/148. Loss or corruption of unchanged active requirements stayed at 1/365 overall. These are descriptive counts, not evidence of noninferiority.

Source-error decisions fell from 59/200 to 26/200; source-error operations fell from 59/238 to 27/230. Both adapters had 0/200 rejected outputs, 0/200 unsupported-addition decisions and 0/13 false updates on true no-change inputs. Duplicate units fell from 4 to 0 and identity-error decisions from 5 to 0. Better citation and structural outcomes do not establish complete intent recovery.

Companion regressions remain: fully correct uncertain requirements fell from 18/24 to 14/24; uncertain concepts omitted increased from 1 to 3, wrong uncertain values from 0 to 2 and uncertain-to-active promotions from 5 to 6. Wrongly withdrawn active units increased from 3 to 5; withdrawn units present as active increased from 1 to 2. Error categories can overlap.

Repair by injected fault was mixed: missing-intent targets 5/20 to 6/20; wrong-text targets 7/20 to 8/20; wrong-owner targets 0/20 to 0/20; wrong-status targets 0/10 to 2/10; mistaken-withdrawal targets 2/5 to 0/5; stale-active cancellation targets 5/5 to 4/5. These small descriptive subgroups identify continuing failures, without isolating their causes.

The adapter-disabled control had 3.74% family-average omission, 23/80 complete repairs and 538/631 fully correct active units. Thus v2's lower omission relative to the base coexisted with fewer complete repairs (20/80 versus 23/80). A favorable secondary omission comparison cannot substitute for the inconclusive primary v2-versus-v1 result.
limits: Data and semantic reviews are model-authored, not human gold. The two late reference corrections demonstrate residual label risk; independent model agreement and file hashes do not prove semantic correctness.

Most scenarios contain six to seven events and share a five-decision authoring pattern. Each decision receives an independently compiled prior state, so errors do not propagate from the model's own earlier state. This is not a natural long-conversation or own-state rollout test.

Training retained 200 old updates and added 300 hard updates informed by exposed v1 failures. Two concrete train/test scenario overlaps were replaced in training before freezing and reviewed again; shared templates and reused older rules remain. Family separation does not prove complete absence of leakage.

The experiment changes the combined data package: scenario mixture, injected prior-state faults, semantic corrections and citation completeness. One seed and no component ablation prevent attributing the observed differences to any one change.

Forty-family bootstrap intervals are approximate and do not account for model-label uncertainty or training-seed variation. Subgroups are small and descriptive; no formal noninferiority test was performed.

Only the tracker role was trained and evaluated. Chat and work roles, dynamic multi-LoRA routing, final delivered answers, ASR and human-user benefit were not evaluated. Five hundred updates are a pilot budget, not an established sufficient data size.
review_note: All 555 unique candidates received an initial blinded model review; 289 received a prospectively selected independent second review. Of the 277 pairs with neither reviewer flagging uncertainty, 253 had identical structured signatures and 24 disagreed; another 12 paired packets had a reviewer flag. In total, 40 current disputes or flags were resolved. Two missing preservation clauses in the original reference labels were confirmed before aggregation and independently approved for an all-arm text-only overlay. Six candidate packets were affected: seven reviewer assignments were re-reviewed and 837 unchanged review assignments were carried forward byte for byte. The adjudicator carried forward its 40 unchanged prior resolved cases after exact packet and 76 included initial-judgment comparisons; it did not claim new semantic reviews of those cases. Original labels, findings, outputs and unsuccessful review submissions remain preserved. The original data card describes pre-training admission; the separate correction disclosure records these later reference defects.
collection_note: The collection journal records 600 physical starts and 600 completed durable assignments in one process, with no failed generation, unresolved start, retry, restart or token-cap hit. All 15 rejected patches occurred with the adapter disabled and retained the prior state for scoring. Each arm consumed 224,369 input tokens; output totals were 11,091 / 9,264 / 9,335 for disabled / v1 / v2. Mean completed-call times were 3.50 / 4.47 / 5.49 seconds. These are descriptive generation times, not end-to-end agent latency; a saved journal cannot prove the absence of unrecorded calls.
training_note: V2 completed one epoch: 500 microsteps and 32 optimizer updates, including the final four-example accumulation group. Both versions used 500 examples and the same optimizer recipe, but actual training tokens differed: v1 628,379 total and 27,728 target tokens; v2 635,990 total and 31,031 target tokens. Recorded training times were 1,672.21 and 1,684.81 seconds. This is an example-budget comparison, not equal-token or equal-FLOP training. The final checkpoint was predetermined; test outputs were not used to retrain or choose a checkpoint.
old_pilot_diagnostic_note: The earlier pilot's wrong-prior regression motivated the revised curriculum. Its subsequent 6/10-to-3/10 repair diagnosis was post hoc and is not a new primary endpoint or fresh held-out result. Earlier frozen results and evidence remain available.
index_text: 600 outputs on 40 fresh families: omission 2.71% to 2.06%, complete repair 19/80 to 20/80; both adjusted primary intervals cross zero, with uncertainty and withdrawal regressions.
next_step: A proposed next study should independently adjudicate matched examples that require owner correction, restoration after mistaken withdrawal and preservation of uncertainty, then freeze a new test set and evaluate state propagation over real multi-turn trajectories. This proposal is not a completed experiment.
